extraction.name: MMMU
extraction.description: MMMU is a comprehensive benchmark designed to evaluate multimodal foundation models on massive multi-discipline tasks demanding college-level subject knowledge and deliberate reasoning. It comprises 11.5K multimodal questions collected from college exams, quizzes, and textbooks across 6 core disciplines, 30 subjects, and 183 subfields, featuring 30 heterogeneous image types and interleaved text-image inputs.
extraction.creator: Xiang Yue, Yuansheng Ni, Kai Zhang, Tianyu Zheng, Ruoqi Liu, Ge Zhang, Samuel Stevens, Dongfu Jiang, Weiming Ren, Yuxuan Sun, Cong Wei, Botao Yu, Ruibin Yuan, Renliang Sun, Ming Yin, Boyuan Zheng, Zhenzhu Yang, Yibo Liu, Wenhao Huang, Huan Sun, Yu Su, Wenhu Chen
extraction.rai:dataCollection: Data collection occurred in three stages: First, selecting subjects from common university majors where visual inputs provide valuable information. Second, recruiting over 50 college students (including coauthors) across various disciplines to collect multimodal questions from major textbooks, lecture materials, and online resources, creating new questions based on their expertise where necessary. Annotators selected questions without immediately available answers to mitigate data contamination, while adhering to copyright and license regulations. Third, quality control and cleaning were performed, resulting in 11.5K final questions.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: College exams, quizzes, textbooks, lecture materials, and free online resources across 30 university subjects.
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: Data cleaning included: 1) identifying and eliminating potential duplicate problems using lexical overlap and source URL similarity followed by author review; 2) format and typo checking distributed among co-authors ensuring standardized JSON format; 3) categorizing problems into four difficulty levels and excluding approximately 10% of problems classified as 'very easy' that did not meet college-level criteria.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Annotators collected and categorized questions as multiple-choice (single correct option) or open-ended (factoid, fill-in-the-blank, calculation-based, short descriptive). They annotated question text, options, correct answers, image types, difficulty level, and explanations if available, inserting images as file paths. Ambiguous cases were flagged and reviewed in team meetings, followed by secondary review and regular audits.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationPlatform: A user-friendly web interface developed by the authors for data annotation and verification.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: Data quality control involved secondary review and regular audits of random samples. Suspicious duplicates flagged via URL similarity and lexical overlap were manually checked. Ambiguities were examined collaboratively in team meetings to standardize annotation.
extraction.rai:annotatorDemographics: Over 50 college students, including co-authors, specializing in diverse university majors and subjects across Art & Design, Business, Science, Health & Medicine, Humanities & Social Science, and Tech & Engineering.
extraction.rai:dataReleaseMaintenancePlan: A live-updating leaderboard is maintained at https://mmmu-benchmark.github.io/#leaderboard, with versions tracked via changelogs (V1 through V4) documenting model additions and case corrections.
extraction.rai:personalSensitiveInformation: Annotators were instructed to comply with privacy laws and ethical standards by explicitly avoiding collecting questions that contain any private information.
extraction.rai:dataSocialImpact: Discusses monitoring progress towards Level 3 / Expert AGI ('at least 90th percentile of skilled adults'), which represents a substitution threshold for machine intelligence in lieu of human labor across industries, carrying potential societal risks of job displacement and economic disruption.
extraction.rai:dataBiases: The manual curation process may carry biases.
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: The manual curation process may carry biases, and the focus on college-level subjects might not be sufficient on its own to test Expert AGI, as there lacks a direct mapping between benchmark performance and the 90th percentile of skilled adults, nor are college exams the only tasks an AGI must tackle.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: Zero-shot and few-shot evaluation / benchmarking of Large Multimodal Models (LMMs) and Large Language Models (LLMs) on college-level multi-discipline multimodal understanding, perception, and reasoning.
